text: When a shared SpecDeck session misbehaves, two tools tell you why: the Connection status panel, and a diagnostics file you can attach to a bug report.
Open the panel from the Help menu, Connection Status, or press Shift Command D.
The top line sums it up in plain words. Here, two viewers are connected, one of them through the relay.
Each viewer gets its own rows: whether it connects directly or through the relay, how much was sent, and how much is still waiting to send.
The terminal and window sections describe the state of your screen. Never what is on it.
To report a problem, click Export Diagnostics, and choose where to save the file.
The file holds the last seven days of connection events and timings. No terminal output, no timeline, no invite codes, names, paths or addresses. Nothing is sent anywhere; you attach it yourself.
Viewers have the same panel. It shows the connection path, and why the previous attempt ended.
If the connection seems stuck, Reconnect drops it and connects again at once, keeping your place.
For a problem that is hard to catch, turn on Verbose logging in Settings. It also records how much each connection sends per second, but never what is sent.
Then reproduce the problem, export the diagnostics, and attach the file to your bug report.
